title: The Missing Lunchbox
story:
At noon Samir could not find his blue lunchbox. He had left it on the classroom shelf by the window. Inside were a sandwich, an apple, and a note from his father. The shelf was empty. He asked the class, and nobody had moved it. Then he saw a trail of tiny apple seeds on the floor. The seeds led into the hallway and stopped at the lost-and-found table.

A blue box sat on that table, but the label said Sami, not Samir. A girl from the next class, Sami Ortega, was eating a sandwich that looked like his. Samir felt upset and was ready to accuse her. Their teacher asked both students to stop and open the boxes. Sami's box was blue and old. Samir's box was blue and new, and it was under a coat on a nearby chair. The coat belonged to a classmate who had not seen the box.

The apple seeds had fallen from Sami's snack while she walked. Samir's note was still inside his own box. He laughed with relief. Samir thanked Sami for waiting while the teacher checked. The two names were almost the same, and the colour had fooled him. He moved his lunchbox to the front of the shelf, where he could see it. Before the next lunch he wrote his full name in large letters on the lid.

A flat board on a wall for storing things.
A line of marks you can follow.
A small paper that shows a name.
To say that someone did something wrong.
A good feeling when a worry ends.

quiz.question: Where had Samir left his lunchbox?
options: On the classroom shelf by the window
On the lost-and-found table
Under a coat in the hall
In the next classroom
quiz.correctAnswer: On the classroom shelf by the window
quiz.explanation: He had left it on the classroom shelf by the window.
quiz.supportingSentence: He had left it on the classroom shelf by the window.

quiz.question: What three things were in his box?
options: A sandwich, an apple, and a note
Only a line of apple seeds
A blue label and a coat
Cookies and a school letter
quiz.correctAnswer: A sandwich, an apple, and a note
quiz.explanation: His box held a sandwich, an apple, and a note from his father.
quiz.supportingSentence: Inside were a sandwich, an apple, and a note from his father.

quiz.question: Where was Samir's own box found?
options: Under a coat on a nearby chair
On the lost-and-found table
In Sami's hands
Beside the window shelf
quiz.correctAnswer: Under a coat on a nearby chair
quiz.explanation: His newer blue box was under a coat on a nearby chair.
quiz.supportingSentence: Samir's box was blue and new, and it was under a coat on a nearby chair.

quiz.question: In this story, what does accuse mean?
options: To say someone did something wrong
To eat lunch in the hallway
To write a name on a lid
To thank a classmate
quiz.correctAnswer: To say someone did something wrong
quiz.explanation: Samir was ready to accuse Sami, or say she had done something wrong.
quiz.supportingSentence: Samir felt upset and was ready to accuse her.

quiz.question: Why did Samir write his full name on the lid?
options: He wanted to prevent the same mix-up
The teacher told him to share the apple
Sami asked him for a new box
The coat had already hidden his name
quiz.correctAnswer: He wanted to prevent the same mix-up
quiz.explanation: The similar names and the blue colour had fooled him, so he made his name easy to see.
quiz.supportingSentence: Before the next lunch he wrote his full name in large letters on the lid.
